name: Senna
short: A case report links years of heavy use to liver failure; chronic abuse may cause fluid and electrolyte loss. A review found no convincing evidence of a link with colon cancer.
text: A case report describes acute liver failure with kidney impairment in a woman who had drunk a litre of senna tea daily for more than 3 years; the authors noted that chronic abuse may also cause fluid and electrolyte loss with chronic diarrhoea, and that severe liver toxicity is unusual. A review of 43 publications found no convincing evidence that stimulant laxatives, including senna, are associated with colon cancer, and judged the cell changes seen at doses above the therapeutic range to be reversible. A review of long-term senna use in children found abdominal cramping or diarrhoea in the first weeks and, rarely, a blistering rash after prolonged skin contact with stool. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
